mainTopic: רבי יהושע's solution for a מצורע whose offerings were mixed up, and רב ששת's challenge to שמואל's explanation of it
overview: This amud opens with the end of רבי יהושע's answer about a man who remarries his divorced wife. From the פסוק he learns that the woman herself is a תועבה, but her children are not. Next comes a new question: two מצורעים had their offerings mixed up, one offering was brought, and then one man died. רבי יהושע says the survivor should give away his property, become poor, and bring a bird חטאת, which may be brought even on a doubt. The גמרא asks what happens with the animal אשם, and שמואל answers that the case is one where the אשם was already brought. רב ששת attacks שמואל's answer from two sides, using a משנה that records which offering decides whether a מצורע counts as rich or poor. Under רבי יהודה, an אשם brought while rich locks him into rich offerings, so the bird חטאת fails. Under רבי שמעון, the survivor could simply bring a new אשם with a condition, so שמואל's limit is not needed. A ברייתא proves that רבי שמעון allows bringing an אשם with a condition, and its next detail continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Only the woman is called an abomination, not her children
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע finishes his answer: the פסוק calls the remarried woman herself a תועבה, so her children are not affected.
steps.simpleTranslation: She is an abomination, but her children are not abominations.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the closing line of רבי יהושע's answer to an earlier question. He reads the פסוק about a man who remarries his divorced wife and shows that the word תועבה is about her alone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'for that (היא) is an abomination', using a word that points to the woman herself. From this he learns that the label does not pass down to her children. So a daughter from such a marriage is not disqualified from marrying a כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: Abomination; the Torah's word for this forbidden remarriage
Her children
A man who takes back his divorced wife after she married someone else, which the Torah forbids

steps.whatToRemember: The forbidden remarriage makes the woman herself a תועבה, but her children keep full status.

phrases.english: She is an abomination,
phrases.notes: This comes from דברים 24:4. The word 'היא' points to the woman herself.

phrases.english: but her children are not abominations.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי יהושע's answer to the earlier question about the daughter of a remarried divorcee.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The daughter is not disqualified, because the פסוק limits the word תועבה to the woman herself.

steps.title: Two lepers whose offerings got mixed up, and then one died
steps.stepSummary: A new question is asked of רבי יהושע: how can the surviving מצורע finish his purification when the offerings were mixed and his partner died?
steps.simpleTranslation: Two מצורעים had their offerings mixed up with each other. The offering of one of them was brought, and then one of them died. What should the second one do?
steps.whatsHappening: The people of Alexandria ask רבי יהושע a new practical question. It is about a מצורע who is stuck and cannot finish becoming טהור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If both men were alive, each could bring the leftover animal with the condition 'for whoever owns it'. Now one is dead, and a חטאת cannot be brought for a dead person, so the leftover animal cannot be used. The survivor also cannot bring a new animal, because the one already offered may have been his, and he cannot bring a second animal חטאת on a doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: A person with צרעת, who must bring offerings to become טהור
Offerings brought in the בית המקדש
Got mixed up, so no one knows which belongs to whom
What will happen with him? How can he solve his problem?

steps.confusionAlert: The problem is not just which animal belongs to whom. Because one owner died and the offering is an animal חטאת, every normal option is blocked.

phrases.english: Two lepers
whose offerings became mixed up with each other,
and the offering of one of them was brought,
and then one of them died.
What shall be with the second one?

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁנֵי מְצוֹרָעִין שֶׁנִּתְעָרְבוּ קׇרְבְּנוֹתֵיהֶן זֶה בָּזֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question put to רבי יהושע, unrelated to the previous one.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the surviving מצורע can complete his offerings when the mix-up and the death block every normal option.

steps.title: Become poor and bring a bird offering
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע answers: the survivor should give his property away, become an עני, and bring a bird חטאת, which may be brought even on a doubt.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: He writes his property over to others and becomes poor. Then he brings a bird חטאת, which may be brought even when there is a doubt.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע gives a clever way out. By becoming poor, the מצורע is allowed to bring a bird חטאת instead of an animal one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A poor מצורע brings birds instead of animals for his חטאת and עולה. A bird חטאת is allowed even when it is not certain that one is needed. An animal חטאת is not. So even if the animal already offered was really his, bringing an extra bird חטאת does no harm.

keyTerms.meaning: He writes over his property to other people, so he no longer owns it
A poor person, who brings cheaper offerings
A חטאת brought from a bird
That may be brought even when there is a doubt

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the rules for a poor person's bird offering can open a door that the rules for animal offerings keep shut.

phrases.english: He said to them:
phrases.notes: 'He' is רבי יהושע, who is answering the people of Alexandria.

phrases.english: He writes his property over to others,
and he becomes poor,
and he brings a bird sin offering,
which may be brought in a case of doubt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the surviving מצורע.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Become poor so he may bring a bird חטאת, which is allowed on a doubt.

steps.title: But he still needs a guilt offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: even a poor מצורע must bring an animal אשם, so the bird solution does not fully work.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is still the אשם!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יהושע's answer. Becoming poor turns the חטאת into a bird, but it does nothing for the אשם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A poor מצורע still brings a lamb for his אשם, not a bird. An animal offering like that cannot be brought on a doubt. So the survivor seems stuck again regarding his אשם.

keyTerms.meaning: But there is still; a challenge pointing out something left out
Guilt offering; for a מצורע it is always an animal, even if he is poor

phrases.english: But there is the guilt offering!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer given in the previous step.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהושע's solution of becoming poor and bringing a bird חטאת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The solution handles only the חטאת. The אשם must still be an animal even for a poor person, and it cannot be brought on a doubt.

steps.title: The guilt offering was already brought
steps.stepSummary: שמואל answers that רבי יהושע was talking about a case where the survivor's אשם had already been offered before the mix-up.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: This is when his אשם had already been brought.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל defends רבי יהושע by narrowing the case. The mix-up happened only with the remaining offerings, after the אשם was already done.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the אשם was already brought, the only open problem is the חטאת. Becoming poor and bringing a bird חטאת then solves the whole case. The challenge is answered by defining the case more exactly, not by changing the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: When his guilt offering had already been brought
Setting the earlier statement in a specific case so that it works

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהושע's solution works because the אשם was already brought, so only the חטאת remained, and that can be a bird for a poor person.

phrases.english: Shmuel said:
When his guilt offering had already been sacrificed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge about the אשם.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the survivor still needed to bring an animal אשם on a doubt, which is not allowed.
steps.terutzMaskana: The case is one where his אשם was already brought, so only the חטאת is left, and the bird solution works.

steps.title: רב ששת attacks שמואל's answer using רבי יהודה's view
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת asks how שמואל could say this. According to רבי יהודה, once the אשם was brought while the person was rich, it locks him into a rich man's offerings, so he cannot later bring a poor man's bird חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: Would a great man like שמואל really say something like this? Whose view would it follow? If it follows רבי יהודה, who says the אשם fixes the status, there is a problem. Since the אשם fixed his status while he was rich, he cannot bring a poor man's חטאת.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת challenges שמואל's answer from Step 5. He starts by testing it against the view of רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל said the survivor's animal אשם was already offered, and then he became poor so he could bring a bird חטאת. But according to רבי יהודה, the אשם decides the level of all the later offerings. An אשם brought while rich means he must bring rich offerings, so becoming poor afterward does not help.

keyTerms.meaning: Fixes or locks in the status for the remaining offerings
Guilt offering, which a מצורע must bring as an animal
Sin offering, which a poor מצורע may bring as a bird
Being wealthy
Being poor

steps.confusionAlert: רב ששת is not saying שמואל's facts are wrong. He is saying that under each major view, שמואל's special case either fails or is not needed.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:
A great man like Shmuel
would say a thing like this?
phrases.notes: He is reacting to שמואל's answer from the last step, that the survivor's אשם was already offered.

phrases.english: In line with whom?
If like Rabbi Yehuda, who said:
"The guilt offering fixes [the status]",
then since the guilt offering fixed it for him while he was wealthy,
he cannot bring a sin offering of a poor person.

steps.triggerLanguage: גַּבְרָא רַבָּה כִּשְׁמוּאֵל לֵימָא כִּי הַאי מִילְּתָא
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's claim that the case is where the אשם was already offered
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to רבי יהודה, an אשם brought while rich locks in rich offerings, so a later bird חטאת is not allowed.

steps.title: The משנה on which offering fixes rich or poor status
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת brings the משנה that records three views on a מצורע whose money situation changed midway. רבי שמעון says the חטאת decides, רבי יהודה says the אשם decides, and רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says the birds decide.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: A מצורע who brought a poor man's offering and then became rich, or brought a rich man's offering and then became poor, everything follows the חטאת. These are the words of רבי שמעון. רבי יהודה says: everything follows the אשם. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says: everything follows the birds.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת quotes the source for רבי יהודה's view that he just used. The same משנה also gives רבי שמעון's view, which he will use next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each sage picks a different offering as the moment that decides whether the מצורע counts as rich or poor. For רבי יהודה it is the אשם, which is why Step 6 said an אשם brought while rich blocks a poor man's חטאת. For רבי שמעון it is the חטאת itself, which sets up the next challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: The cheaper offering a poor מצורע brings, with birds in place of some animals
He became wealthy
He became poor
Everything follows; the status at that offering decides the rest
The birds offered at the very start of the מצורע's purification

steps.whyThisMatters: This משנה is the key behind the whole challenge. Which offering decides the status determines whether שמואל's case can work.

phrases.english: As we learned in a mishna:
A leper who brought a poor person's offering
and then became wealthy, or [brought] a wealthy person's offering and then became poor
everything follows the sin offering;
these are the words of Rabbi Shimon.
And Rabbi Yehuda says:
Everything follows the guilt offering.
Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov says:
Everything follows the birds.
phrases.notes: These are the birds brought seven days earlier, at the start of his purification.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for רבי יהודה's view used in Step 6
steps.raayaObject: That according to רבי יהודה the אשם fixes the status

steps.title: Under רבי שמעון, שמואל's special case is unnecessary
steps.stepSummary: If רבי יהושע follows רבי שמעון, where the חטאת decides the status, then even if the אשם was never offered, the survivor could simply bring another אשם with a condition. רבי שמעון is known to allow 'bring and stipulate.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it follows רבי שמעון, who says the חטאת fixes the status, then even if the אשם was not yet offered, let him bring another one. For we have heard that רבי שמעון said: let him bring it and make a condition.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת finishes his challenge with the second option, רבי שמעון. Under this view, שמואל's limit to a case where the אשם was already offered is not needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With רבי שמעון the poor man's bird חטאת is fine, because the חטאת itself decides the status. The only remaining problem is the missing אשם, and רבי שמעון allows bringing a new animal with a condition to cover the doubt. So there was no reason for שמואל to say the אשם had already been offered.

keyTerms.meaning: Let him bring an offering and make a condition about what it counts as
Let him bring another one
Even though

steps.whatToRemember: רב ששת's challenge has two sides. Under רבי יהודה, שמואל's case does not work. Under רבי שמעון, שמואל's case is not needed.

phrases.english: And if like Rabbi Shimon, who said:
the sin offering fixes [the status],

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא קְרַב אָשָׁם
phrases.english: then even if the guilt offering was not offered
let him bring another,
for we have heard of Rabbi Shimon
that he said: Let him bring and stipulate.
phrases.notes: He sets a condition: the animal is his אשם if he still needs one, and otherwise it counts as a different offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, דְּאָמַר: חַטָּאת קָבְעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second side of רב ששת's challenge, using רבי שמעון's view from the משנה in Step 7
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's need to limit the case to an אשם already offered
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under רבי שמעון, the survivor can just bring a new אשם with a condition, so the limit is unnecessary.

steps.title: Proof that רבי שמעון allows bringing an offering with a condition
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows רבי שמעון letting a doubtful מצורע bring an אשם with a condition: if he is a מצורע it is his אשם, and if not it becomes a voluntary שלמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches, רבי שמעון says: On the next day he brings his guilt offering and his לוג of oil with it. He stands at שער ניקנור and makes a condition about the animal, saying: 'If he is a מצורע, here is his guilt offering and his לוג with it. If not, this guilt offering should be a voluntary peace offering.' And that guilt offering requires...
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת proves what he said in Step 8: רבי שמעון really does allow someone to bring a sacrifice with a condition attached. The last words start the ברייתא's next detail, which continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 claimed that according to רבי שמעון, the survivor could just bring a new אשם with a condition. This ברייתא shows רבי שמעון doing exactly that for a person who is not sure he is a מצורע. One animal works either way: it is an אשם if he needs one, and a voluntary שלמים if he does not.

keyTerms.meaning: A measure of oil that the מצורע brings along with his אשם
The Nicanor Gate, the eastern gate of the עזרה, where the מצורע stands during his purification
Makes a condition, attaching an 'if this, then that' to the offering
A voluntary peace offering

steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא is the source showing that רבי שמעון allows 'bring and stipulate.' That is what makes רב ששת's question in Step 8 so strong against שמואל's explanation, that the אשם had already been offered.

phrases.english: As it is taught: Rabbi Shimon says:
On the next day he brings his guilt offering
phrases.notes: 'The next day' is the eighth day of the מצורע's purification, when his offerings are brought.

phrases.english: and his log of oil with it,
and he stands him at the Nicanor Gate,
and he makes a condition about it and says:
If he is a metzora,
phrases.notes: He is speaking about himself here, as if about a third person.

phrases.english: here is his guilt offering and his log with it,
and if not,
this guilt offering shall be a voluntary peace offering.
And that guilt offering requires

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the claim in Step 8 that רבי שמעון allows 'bring and stipulate.'
steps.raayaObject: The claim that רבי שמעון holds one may bring an offering with a condition (מביא ומתנה)
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא where רבי שמעון has a doubtful מצורע bring an אשם stipulating that it is an אשם if he is a מצורע, and otherwise a שלמי נדבה
